newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares settle at higher levels in late IBIS.
newsitem.headline: German shares settle at higher levels in late IBIS.

text.p: German shares tread water in late electronic trade on Friday, still in record territory but shy of the magic 2,800 point threshold, with trade underpinned by a stronger dollar and a strong start on Wall Street.

At 1513 GMT the IBIS DAX index stood at 2,789.91 points, up 5.52 points. The IBIS DAX hit an all-time high of 2,798.24 points earlier in the day, tantalisingly near the 2,800-point threshold, but lacking the necessary impetus to breach it.
"It's really selected stocks which have driven up the market today, particularly the banks and stocks like Metro and Daimler," said one trader.
The big event of the coming week is the flotation of Deutsche Telekom on Monday, which will be Europe's biggest-ever flotation.
Market players are anticipating huge volumes when the shares launch on Monday, with around 3.6 billion shares in Deutsche Telekom ordered by the close of the subscription period on Thursday.

Banking sources said the issue would be oversubscribed six times. Telekom shares traded at 33.50 in the grey market on Friday, 11.66 percent above the top of the expected range of 25-30 marks set last month.

The banks were the focus of attention over the day and the top three banks -- Deutsche Bank, Dresdner Bank and Commerzbank -- featured all day in the list of most heavily-traded shares after merger/takeover speculation.
Commerzbank was down 15 pfennigs at 36.50 marks amid profit-taking, while Deutsche was up 27 pfennigs at 72.38 marks and Dresdner Bank was up 32 pfennigs at 44.90 marks.
Good support also came from the Bund future, which stood at 100.97 points in late trade, off earlier highs of 101.14 points, but still seen supportive.
